title: Asahi to invest 13.5 billion yen in cybersecurity over three years after 2025 ransomware attack
date_note: Nikkei Asia page is stamped 21 November 03:59 JST (20 November UTC); the date is the publication day.
summary: Nikkei Asia reports that Asahi Group Holdings will invest 13.5 billion yen ($85 million) in cybersecurity over three years. The lede says the money is for rebuilding systems using AI and more specialized talent to detect unauthorized access. A photo caption says CEO Atsushi Katsuki detailed the plans after a ransomware attack last year that disrupted business for months.
plain: Asahi, after a 2025 ransomware attack that disrupted business for months, will invest 13.5 billion yen ($85 million) over three years in cybersecurity, per Nikkei Asia.
exec: Asahi's reported 13.5 billion yen ($85 million) three-year cybersecurity plan follows a ransomware attack that disrupted business for months.
geo_basis: company headquarters; article read only in part

validation.note: Single publisher (Nikkei Asia); only the headline, subhead and lede were readable, the body was not.
